concepts.label: Distributed ACID Transaction - a multi-document, multi-operation unit of work executed via a retryable lambda passed to `Cluster.transactions().run()`, automatically committed on success or rolled back and retried on failure

concepts.label: TransactionAttemptContext (`ctx`) - the transaction-scoped CRUD/query API (ctx.insert/get/replace/remove/query) whose writes are staged and invisible to other actors until the transaction commits
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - structurally distinct concurrency-control primitive from sdk:cas-optimistic-locking. The page states replace/remove require a prior ctx.get() 'so the SDK can check that the document is not involved in another transaction, and take appropriate action if so' - this is a transaction-membership check, not a CAS-token comparison. concepts.label: Transaction-scoped Durability Level - a single DurabilityLevel setting (Majority / MajorityAndPersistToActive / PersistToMajority / None) that applies to every key-value write inside one transaction attempt, configured once via TransactionsConfig/ClusterEnvironment rather than per individual mutation call
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - deliberately NOT reused as sdk:durability. sdk:durability (kv-operations.md) is a per-operation option passed to an individual insert/upsert/replace call; this setting is per-transaction (or global, via ClusterEnvironment), applying uniformly to every write the transaction performs, and is configured through a completely different API surface (TransactionsConfig.durabilityLevel(...) vs InsertOptions.durability(...)). The underlying enum values are literally the same, so I related the two concepts via sharesOptionSetWith rather than treating them as unrelated, but the SCOPE is structurally different, exactly as the batch hypothesis anticipated.

relations.evidence: The default configuration will perform all writes with the durability setting `Majority`, ensuring that each write is available in-memory on the majority of replicas before the transaction continues. There are two higher durability settings available that will additionally wait for all mutations to be written to physical storage on either the active or the majority of replicas, before continuing.

relations.subject: sdk:distributed-transaction
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate captures a mid-flow permission-scope switch triggered by an operation type
relations.evidence: When a transaction executes a query statement, the transaction enters **query mode**, which means that the query is executed with the user's query permissions. Any **key-value** operations which are executed by the transaction _after_ the query statement are _also_ executed with the user's query permissions. These may or may not be different to the user's data permissions; if they are different, you may get unexpected results.

notable_absence.finding: The 'Refer to Error Handling' link on this page points to concept-docs/transactions-error-handling.md, NOT to howtos/error-handling.md (the general SDK error-handling page extracted earlier in this batch). Re-checking that page confirms it contains zero mentions of TransactionFailedException, TransactionCommitAmbiguousException, or transactions of any kind. Transactions have their own, entirely separate error-handling documentation branch.

cross_component_finding: This page is the strongest evidence in the batch for the round's hypothesis: transactions do NOT extend cleanly into the existing per-operation SDK vocabulary. (1) Concurrency control: sdk:cas-optimistic-locking (per-op CAS token comparison) has no role here - ctx.replace()/ctx.remove() require a prior ctx.get() purely to check transaction membership ('the SDK can check that the document is not involved in another transaction'), a fundamentally different mechanism, so I minted sdk:transaction-attempt-context rather than reusing CAS. (2) Durability: sdk:durability is a per-call option; this page's durability setting is configured once (via TransactionsConfig/ClusterEnvironment, or per-single-query-transaction in the next page) and silently applies to every write in the transaction attempt - same enum values, different and incompatible scope, so I minted sdk:transaction-durability and linked it back via sharesOptionSetWith rather than reusing sdk:durability directly. (3) Two entirely new behaviors with no per-operation analogue at all: Query Mode (permission scope silently shifts mid-transaction once any query runs) and the whole-transaction commit-ambiguity exception pair (TransactionFailedException/TransactionCommitAmbiguousException, documented on a separate page from the general exception hierarchy). This matches the shape the hypothesis predicted by analogy to Sync Gateway's channel model in round 3 - a genuinely new structural layer, not a relabeling of existing primitives.
cross_product_finding: The Capella-vs-self-managed-Server prerequisite tabs on this page diverge in a way I haven't seen elsewhere in the SDK batches so far: Capella's prerequisites drop the minimum-server-version requirement entirely (Capella prereqs just say 'Couchbase Capella account') and drop the NTP-sync requirement, both of which are explicit for self-managed Server. I reused deployment:capella (minted in the cloud/n1ql round) for this rather than edition:enterprise/edition:community, since this is a deployment-model distinction (managed vs self-managed), not a licensing-tier distinction - consistent with how alterindex.json used the same object for a similar Capella-only-behavior case.
